description:
Investigated on develop + #401 (3038a76af); report /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/report.md (Parts 1 and 2), hand answer /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/hand.md, page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.127.html.

The earlier text of this ticket named the protocol callback rule (visit_protocol_callback keys non-receiver arguments Whole) as the cause. Measured, it accounts for none of the key growth: setting it to Class removed no key on the k-site series and widened Enum.member?/2's result on the OptionParser probes. That rule stays as it is.

Defect. Two Enum.reduce sites over one any-typed value, one with an int accumulator and one with a map: the compiler reports spec/violation +/2 (%{}, int), because site 0's closure is analysed with site 1's accumulator. It reproduces with a user-written wrapper struct, compose function and Enumerable impl and no Stream (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/p2/w.fz), on a lib with the Stream impl deleted, and with the stream-flatten library change applied. Condition: the receiver is typed any.

First wrong decision. Both sites' calls to the compose function share one activation key, because the nested closure is folded to fun (fold_self_nested_closures, types/mod.rs ~4611, via world.rs ~2384). The activation keeps one input row per site, each analysed correctly. The caller then reads the activation's single return, the join of all rows, in prepare_function_call (jobs/semantic.rs ~2234-2240). The union of both sites' closures flows on and is paired with each site's accumulator.

Second, behind it. With that union gone, Enum.reduce/3#lambda@0/2 is still keyed with site 0's closure and site 1's accumulator; the call surfaces come from plan_callable_flows (runtime_demand.rs ~1043-1110) and ground_dispatch_surfaces (semantic.rs ~635-665), which has no per-site filter. The edge carrying the foreign surface is not established.

Rule to hold: a caller may read a shared activation but receives the return its own inputs produce.

Tried and rejected: keeping the innermost closure's identity in the folded key instead of fun (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/spike_keepleaf_v1.diff): keys 2,459 -> 2,232 at 8 sites, the wrong diagnostic persists.

Not yet spiked: per-row returns at prepare_function_call; a per-site filter for call surfaces. Open: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/p2/w2.fz (a reducer wrapped in a closure each lap, no compose) did not terminate in 20 minutes.

Acceptance: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/p2/w.fz compiles and matches elixir on interp, run and build; the k = 1, 2, 4, 8 series (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/gen.py) grows linearly in keys; the distiller (tools/distill-telemetry.exs) needs fewer than 50,000 product requests without touching the budget (63,457 with the stream-flatten change alone); jobs do not rise on the five OptionParser probes; no rule that depends on which implementations have landed; no cap, budget or cache. Do not build before the spike's numbers are on a page.

The library half (a stream wrapping a stream reduces as one stream, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/k127/spike_streamflat.diff) is separate work and is not this ticket.
title: A call reads the return its own inputs produce, not the join of every caller's row
